One wrong holiday calendar can misdate many payments; one incorrect CSA mapping can change margining; one stale settlement instruction can generate repeated fails. Reconciliation therefore should distinguish a trade break from a shared reference-data break. The BA test is to trace every critical trade field backwards: was it entered on the trade, derived from a mastered object, looked up by effective date, or overwritten manually? That lineage determines both control design and root-cause analysis. ### Permanent rule Master the meaning and effective date of a field before reconciling its value. ### Permanent trap Using ticker, short name or free text as a durable cross-system identifier. ### Never confuse **Reference data** — descriptive or classificatory data used repeatedly to interpret transactions and processes. --- **Transaction data** — data recording a specific business event or position. ### Jurisdiction variants **No delta.**

title: The Derivatives Documentation Stack
one_screen: Derivative documentation is layered: a master agreement sets relationship-wide legal rules, schedules customise them, credit-support documents govern collateral and confirmations define individual transactions. The economic trade cannot be understood safely from the confirmation alone.
bodyText: OTC derivatives are documented through a stack rather than one self-contained trade ticket. The master agreement establishes relationship-wide legal terms such as payment mechanics, events of default, termination events, representations and close-out. A negotiated schedule amends or supplements the standard master terms for the two parties. Credit-support documentation addresses collateral. Under ISDA relationships, a Credit Support Annex or other credit-support document defines eligible collateral, thresholds, minimum transfer amounts, valuation, haircuts and transfer mechanics. These collateral terms affect exposure, liquidity and valuation. Individual transactions are then recorded in confirmations that specify product economics: notional, dates, fixed rates, floating-rate options, strikes, settlement and other terms. Confirmations frequently incorporate published definitional booklets rather than restating every calculation rule. For interest-rate derivatives, the 2021 ISDA Interest Rate Derivatives Definitions are a major modern reference framework. The “single agreement” concept under ISDA connects transactions legally under the master framework. That architecture is crucial for close-out netting because a default can lead to termination and calculation of a relationship-level net amount under the applicable agreement. Product-specific financing markets use other master agreements. Repo is commonly documented under the GMRA; securities lending under the GMSLA. Those should not be replaced casually by an ISDA label because legal form and product mechanics differ. For data design, contract identity is therefore separate from trade identity. A trade should map to the correct master agreement, schedule, collateral agreement and definitional version. Amendments must be effective-dated. If a relationship is repapered, historical trades may remain under old terms while new trades use new terms. The practical question is: which document controls this field? Economic data may come from the confirmation; close-out rights from the master; collateral thresholds from the CSA; calculation mechanics from definitions. ### Permanent rule Map every contractual data element to the document that legally controls it. ### Permanent trap Treating the confirmation as the entire legal contract or assuming every OTC product uses the same master agreement. ### Never confuse **Master agreement** — relationship-level legal framework governing multiple transactions. --- **Confirmation** — transaction-level document recording specific economic terms. ### Jurisdiction variants **No delta.**

title: ISDA Master Agreement and Close-Out Netting
one_screen: The ISDA Master Agreement turns many OTC derivatives into one governed relationship. If termination is triggered, close-out netting values the covered terminated transactions and collapses them into a single net amount, subject to the agreement and applicable law.
bodyText: The ISDA Master Agreement is a standard framework for OTC derivatives relationships. The 2002 form updates the 1992 architecture and includes provisions for payment, representations, events of default, termination events, close-out amount and set-off. Parties negotiate elections and amendments in a Schedule. Its central risk-management feature is the relationship between the “single agreement” concept and close-out. In normal conditions, individual transactions continue with their own cash flows. If an Event of Default or relevant Termination Event occurs and the contractual steps are satisfied, transactions can be terminated in accordance with the agreement. Their replacement or close-out values are calculated and combined into one Early Termination Amount under the applicable terms. Close-out netting reduces gross bilateral replacement obligations into a net claim or payable. If one party is owed 100 on some terminated transactions and owes 80 on others, enforceable netting can leave a single 20 claim rather than separate gross obligations. This can materially reduce counterparty exposure and capital requirements where regulatory conditions are met. But netting is a legal conclusion, not an arithmetic feature. Enforceability depends on governing law, counterparty type, insolvency regime, branches and transaction scope. Banks therefore rely on legal opinions and eligibility controls before recognising netting benefits. A database “netting set” flag does not create legal enforceability. Resolution regimes can also impose temporary stays on termination rights for certain financial institutions. ISDA’s close-out framework highlights the interaction among default notices, stays and collateral enforcement. Set-off and close-out netting should not be treated as identical. Close-out netting operates through termination and valuation of covered transactions under the contractual framework; set-off may apply to separate payment obligations under different legal conditions. The operational control is document-to-netting-set lineage: every trade included in a net exposure calculation must be legally in scope. ### Permanent rule Netting benefit exists only if the contractual mechanism is legally enforceable for the relevant parties and transactions. ### Permanent trap Assuming a system-generated net amount proves legal close-out netting eligibility. ### Never confuse **Close-out netting** — termination, valuation and combination of covered transactions into a single net amount. --- **Set-off** — legal combination of mutual payment obligations that may arise under a different basis and scope. ### Jurisdiction variants **No delta.**

title: Credit Support Annex and Collateral
one_screen: A CSA governs collateral for a derivatives relationship. It converts changing mark-to-market exposure into collateral calls according to agreed thresholds, eligible assets, valuation rules and transfer mechanics; it changes counterparty and liquidity risk, not the underlying derivative payoff.
bodyText: A Credit Support Annex, or CSA, sits alongside an ISDA Master Agreement and defines how collateral supports covered derivatives exposure. The exact legal form differs by governing law and document type, but the economic objective is to reduce unsecured counterparty exposure as market values change. Variation margin responds to current exposure. If a portfolio moves in one party’s favour, collateral may be transferred by the out-of-the-money party subject to thresholds, minimum transfer amounts, rounding and timing rules. Initial margin, where applicable, is designed to cover potential future exposure during a close-out period and is often subject to segregation requirements under regulatory frameworks. Eligible collateral can include cash and securities. Non-cash collateral may receive a haircut so that only a discounted value counts. Currency mismatches, concentration limits and wrong-way risk can also affect eligibility or value. Interest or price alignment amounts may be paid on cash collateral according to the agreement. Collateral mechanics have direct valuation consequences. The rate paid on cash collateral influences the economically appropriate discounting framework for collateralised derivatives. A change in CSA currency or remuneration can therefore change fair value even if the trade’s headline fixed rate and notional do not change. A margin call is not the same as settlement of the derivative. It is a collateral lifecycle event. Disputes may arise because counterparties value trades differently, apply different market data or disagree on eligible collateral. Operations must track call amount, agreed amount, disputed amount, collateral delivered, value date and substitutions. Collateral reduces loss given counterparty default but creates liquidity demands. During volatility, a firm can be economically solvent yet face large same-day cash calls. Collateral risk management is therefore both a credit-risk and treasury problem. ### Permanent rule A CSA changes collateralisation of counterparty exposure; it does not rewrite the derivative’s underlying payoff. ### Permanent trap Treating posted collateral as unavailable to liquidity risk merely because it reduces credit exposure. ### Never confuse **Variation margin** — collateral responding primarily to current mark-to-market exposure. --- **Initial margin** — collateral intended primarily to cover potential future exposure during a close-out period. ### Jurisdiction variants **No delta.**

title: Banking Book versus Trading Book
one_screen: The regulatory book boundary determines which capital framework applies to an instrument. Trading intent matters, but modern Basel rules add mandatory classifications, presumptions, documentation and tight restrictions on switching so that banks cannot move positions simply to obtain lower capital.
bodyText: The banking book and trading book are regulatory classifications, not product categories. The same broad instrument type can sit in different books depending on purpose and the applicable mandatory rules. Under the Basel Framework, trading-book instruments are subject to market-risk capital requirements, while banking-book instruments are generally subject to credit-risk capital requirements. The first test is not “is this security tradable?” Basel RBC25 contains mandatory treatments and presumptions. Instruments held for short-term resale, profit from short-term price movements, arbitrage or hedging those trading risks are designated to the trading book subject to the framework. Certain instruments are required in the banking book; others, such as listed equities, market-making positions and trading-related repo-style transactions, are presumed to be trading-book positions unless the conditions for deviation are satisfied. Trading-book eligibility also carries operating expectations. The instrument must not face a legal impediment to sale or full hedging, and Basel requires daily fair valuation with valuation changes recognised in P&L. Banks must maintain documented policies, controls and periodic audit over designation. Reclassification after initial designation is deliberately difficult. Basel prohibits switching for regulatory arbitrage and says moves should be rare and allowed only in extraordinary circumstances. A change in market conditions, liquidity or trading intent alone is not a valid reason. Supervisory approval, senior management approval, documentation and disclosure are required for permitted discretionary reassignments, and a capital benefit from switching is neutralised through a Pillar 1 surcharge. This boundary therefore connects product knowledge to capital, finance, risk and data. A BA needs instrument identity, desk, accounting classification, purpose, regulatory-book designation, approval evidence and effective date. “Held by treasury” or “available for sale” is not a sufficient regulatory-book rule. ### Permanent rule Regulatory-book designation follows the rule framework and documented purpose; it is not a free management choice. ### Permanent trap Moving a capital-intensive or loss-making position between books because the other capital treatment is cheaper. Basel explicitly prohibits regulatory-arbitrage switching. ### Never confuse **Accounting classification** — financial-reporting classification under the applicable accounting framework. --- **Regulatory-book classification** — banking-book or trading-book designation used for prudential capital treatment. ### Jurisdiction variants **IN — Perishable, checked 28 August 2026.** RBI’s 2023 investment-portfolio directions, effective 1 April 2024 for commercial banks excluding RRBs, introduced a clearly identifiable Held for Trading subcategory within FVTPL and removed the earlier 90-day HFT holding ceiling. This accounting/investment classification should not be silently equated with full Basel FRTB implementation; the applicable RBI capital directions must be checked for the capital-boundary treatment in force. **UK — Perishable, checked 28 August 2026.** PRA PS1/26 states that the Basel 3.1 rules and policy, including the revised market-risk framework other than IMA, take effect on 1 January 2027. The market-risk internal model approach takes effect on 1 January 2028. **EU — Perishable, checked 28 August 2026.** On 3 August 2026 the EBA issued a no-action letter recommending that competent authorities not prioritise supervision or enforcement of specified FRTB banking/trading-book boundary and internal-risk-transfer provisions during the implementation adjustment associated with the Commission’s 2026 Delegated Act. **US — Perishable, checked 28 August 2026.** The 2026 federal banking-agency modernised capital and revised market-risk framework remained a proposal rather than a final rule; do not present the proposed Basel-aligned boundary as current US final law.
